q: what happened last wekk that made Creamy Cropman a 1800+ scorer that now his projection is 1411? That's a massive drop off. What on earth could he have done, or what players does he have that will not repeat that again? Seems like a harsh under projection considering his performance last week being the top scorer
short: Last week Creamy Cropmen started 52 player-games at 36 FP each; this week it is 45 starts with Haliburton, Kawhi and Vassell out, and the 1411 projection (31.4 per start) already assumes some regression from a hot week.
answer:
Short version: last week was a volume spike plus a hot streak, and 1411 is less harsh than it looks once you separate the two.

Volume: Creamy Cropmen started 52 player-games last week and scored 1871, which is 36.0 FP per start. This week they have only 45 starts (8, 3, 8, 4, 8, 8, 6 by day), so 7 fewer games. At last week's pace that alone is about 250 FP. Jaden McDaniels and Nolan Traore only play 2 games this week, Tyrese Haliburton and Kawhi Leonard are still on IR producing zero, and Devin Vassell (74 FP in 2 games last week) is now listed OUT.

Hot streak: the projection is 1410.8 over 45 starts, which is 31.4 FP per start. The model had them at only 1402 last week and they beat that by about 470. The players who ran furthest above their projections and are least likely to repeat: Kyshawn George 198 in 4 games (49.5 per game vs a 30.2 projection), Davion Mitchell 172 in 4 (43.0 vs 25.5), Wendell Carter Jr. 122 in 3 (40.7 vs 23.0), Franz Wagner 164 in 3 (54.7 vs 38.6), Aaron Wiggins 114 in 4 (28.5 vs 19.2), and Jalen Smith 90 in 3 (30.0 vs 22.4). Luka Doncic actually ran below his 67.3 season average (214 in 4 games, 53.5 per game).

So the drop is roughly 250 from fewer games and roughly 200 from regression to normal scoring. The projection uses expected per-game averages, so it will not assume another 36 per start week. It could still be a bit low: George (37.2), Mitchell (41.2), Wagner (42.6) and Carter (34.6) all have season averages above their projection numbers. If they play to season averages, I would expect something closer to 1500 to 1650. My honest range is 1400 to 1650, not 1870. For context, Angel Reese is projected 1988 and Nifty Neighbas 1732, so Creamy is a mid-pack team this week rather than the top scorer.

This is about scoring and schedule rather than an injury timeline, so I did not run news searches. The IR and OUT statuses come from the league data.
